name: Glean
tagline: Enterprise AI search and assistant over a company's own docs, chat and apps (permission-aware). The SWE loop is a LeetCode-style technical phone screen (sometimes a practical build), then an onsite with 1-2 coding rounds (one often open-ended and 'practical', where you code mostly on your own for a long stretch), system design and behavioral.
notes: Reported SWE coding questions (2026) mix classic algorithms with search-flavoured practical tasks: simulating documents assigned to parallel indexers (i % m with wrap-around, drops, then a top-k load report), top-k prefix typeahead filtered by the user's department under a tight memory budget, a BPE tokenizer (train with a frequency threshold, then encode/decode), grouping words into synonym sets by shared surrounding context, plus word search in a grid, k-th largest across two sorted arrays, a no-parentheses calculator, 2048 tile moves and OOD chess. One new-grad report describes a 2-hour assignment building a module in stages, where finishing most parts mattered. ML candidates have had a 75-minute AI-assisted build (a rate-limited crawler). Interviewers care about settling the ambiguous rules (ties, boundaries, unknown input) up front, getting a correct baseline before optimising, stating and then improving the complexity, and making steady independent progress in the practical round.
